brief.situation: You are the Azure lead for Pell & Hart, a fictional distributor migrating SAP S/4HANA to Azure (West Europe). Tonight's wave: the target landscape deploys this afternoon, and at 18:00 the database export from the data center starts. The deployment of the two HANA VMs (M64s) just failed. The application server VMs deployed fine.
handover: The subscription is new for this program; nobody has requested quota for it yet.
If the export does not start by 18:00, the wave moves four weeks and the data center contract is extended.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the subscription's quotas in West Europe and the VMs the wave needs.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The database export starts at 18:00, 150 minutes after the failure; the HANA VMs and their preparation need about an hour.

writeup.question: For the record: why the HANA deployment failed, what you did, and how later waves avoid it.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The error said the standardMSFamily quota in westeurope was 0 and 128 vCPUs were needed. The regional total had room; the VM-family tier had none, because nobody had requested quota for the new subscription.

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Requests the right quota and keeps the landscape together.
parts.modelAnswer: Requested 256 MS-family vCPUs in West Europe (approved in minutes, with Professional Direct ready if not) and re-ran the deployment. Deploying in North Europe would have split the app servers and the database across regions.

parts.label: Later waves
parts.criteria: Treats quota as a planning input.
parts.modelAnswer: Requested the families for waves 4-7 now and added a quota check two weeks before each wave.

expertPath.text: Error: standardMSFamily limit 0, need 128; regional total has room; sizing sheet has no quota check; no requests open.
Request 256 in West Europe, re-run; request later waves' families, change the checklist.
Both HANA VMs in West Europe, zones 1 and 2; niping 0.31 ms.

splitRegion.headline: Free quota in the wrong place
splitRegion.body: SAP needs the application servers and the database close together. Moving one tier to another region to dodge quota trades a request of a few minutes for an unsupportable landscape.

wavePostponed.headline: A quota is a planning input
wavePostponed.body: Quotas are per subscription, per region, per VM family. Request them when the subscription is created, and long before a migration window.

deployed.headline: Good: the right limit, in time
deployed.body: You read the error and the usage, saw the family tier (not the region) was the limit, requested it with an escalation path, checked the result and latency, and planned quota for every later wave.

scoring.modelReasoning: The error names the M-series family quota in West Europe: zero, with 128 vCPUs needed, while the regional total has room. Quotas apply per subscription, region and VM family, and both tiers must have room. Request the family quota now, with the support plan ready if it is not fulfilled at once, and re-run; retrying alone changes nothing, and deploying the database in another region splits SAP's tiers. Then request the later waves' quotas and make quota a checklist item.
